result.title: TraCE: Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding
result.summary: Video understanding models often rely on motion, yet their explanations can obscure which motion sources support a prediction. We identify motion-source under-specification as a limitation of existing video XAI: region-centric explanations can be source-ambiguous, while motion vocabularies restricted to single-person pose sequences are source-incomplete. We propose TraCE (Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding), a concept-based framework that discovers source-flexible motion concepts by clustering optical-flow trajectories from training videos. These concepts represent dynamic evidence from people, objects, and interactions, while object and scene concepts account for static context. The resulting typed trajectory/object/scene interface supports class prediction for action recognition and question-conditioned concept matching for video question answering (VQA). We evaluate TraCE across five random seeds on six benchmarks: NTU RGB+D Mutual, Chiral SSv2, UCF-101, KTH, TOMATO, and STAR. Relative to non-interpretable baselines, TraCE maintains competitive task performance, with an average accuracy drop of 1.0 points for action recognition and a nominal gain of 0.4 points for VQA. Motion perturbation and concept-removal tests provide complementary evidence of directional semantic alignment and decision faithfulness, while sample-level interventions illustrate targeted model debugging. Our project page is available at https://leewooil.github.io/TraCE_project_page/.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TraCE，通过聚类训练视频中的光流轨迹发现来源灵活（人、物、交互）的运动概念，并与物体、场景概念构成类型化接口，用于可解释的动作识别与视频问答。
AI.relevance_reason: 其运动扰动与概念移除测试可能为 LVR 中「视觉证据是否被因果使用、如何分配贡献」提供评价思路，但该框架面向视频 XAI，与 latent 推理状态生成的联系仍需核查。
